title: Condensed constant Weil object and compact-support realization
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell\subset\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $a_Y:Y\to s$ be the structure map. Let $E_Y$ be the rationalized constant adic object with the normalized integral model of [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum]. Write $E_T^c=p_T^*\underline E$ and $U_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$ for $T=Y,s$, where $\underline\Omega=\operatorname{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)$ is exactly [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and use the coefficient map $E_T^c\to U_T$ of [def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map]. Let $J_T$ be the adic-to-condensed $E$ realization of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. In the actual module-object category [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], form
$$K=U_Y\otimes^L_{E_Y^c}J_Y(E_Y).$$
Here scalar extension means the derived extension of module objects along the displayed coefficient map [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. There is a canonical isomorphism $J_Y(E_Y)\cong E_Y^c$ and hence $K\cong U_Y$ in degree zero. For the $k$-linear model Frobenius $\Phi$ (the base change of the $q$-power Frobenius of $Y_0$), the unit pullback isomorphism defines $\phi:L\Phi^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. It makes $(K,\phi)$ an actual $\operatorname{WeilBoundedConstructibleOfEnd}\ \ell\ \Phi$ of the coefficient category in [nt-assume-trace-formula], and is the image of the normalized model Weil structure after reconstructing its compatible integral tower, rationalizing it to $E$, applying $J_Y$, and extending from $E_Y^c$ to $U_Y$. Its iterates use the canonical pullback-composition comparisons.

Let $C_E=R\Gamma_c(Y,E_Y)$ be the ordinary $E$-complex of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], which belongs to $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ by the point equivalence of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], and use $\rho_{E,s}$ of [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace]. The canonical compact-support coefficient comparison and point realization give a specified isomorphism in $D^b_c(s)[[\underline\Omega]]$
$$\sigma_Y:Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{cond}}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_{E,s}(C_E),$$
where $Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the chosen-compactification module-object functor of [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek]. On cohomology this gives the internal module $\rho_{E,s}(H_c^i(Y,E)[0])$; its geometric-point value is $H_c^i(Y,E)\otimes_E\Omega$. For every $k$-point $x:s\to Y$, there is a canonical isomorphism $\lambda_x:Lx^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}U_s=\rho_{E,s}(E[0])$. If $\Phi^m\circ x=x$, the stalk operator obtained from $\phi_m$ and this fixed-point equality is carried by $\lambda_x$ to $1_{U_s}$. All the comparisons asserted here concern actual condensed module objects, rather than identifying the adic and condensed coefficient categories by notation. No equality between their global Frobenius operators, and no trace or dualizability assertion, is part of this statement.

source.place: 6.7.14, 6.8.14(2), 6.8.15; agent-formulated constant-object specialization of lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization and lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization, with the exact module-object compact-support functor of upstream master ModuleObject/Derived/BoundedConstructible.lean, lines 268-302; normalization against the cited assumption interface is an additional comparison obligation, not literally stated in Bhatt–Scholze

proof.text: Let $M=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,Y}[0]$. Its actual normalized reduction system, quotient transitions, finite model-Weil maps and rationalization $E_Y$ are those of [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum]. Apply [lem-zl-normalized-coefficient-unit-realization] to $h=\Phi$ and $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Its $j_Y$ identifies $J_Y(E_Y)$ with $E_Y^c$; its $v=u_Y$ identifies $K=T^Y_{E,\Omega}J_Y(E_Y)$ with $U_Y$. If $d_\Phi$ is the integral model map reconstructed from the canonical finite unit multiplications, the lemma gives the actual equation $v\,T^Y_{E,\Omega}J_Y(qd_\Phi)=e_\Phi L\Phi^*(v)c_\Phi$. Consequently its transported map is exactly $\phi=v^{-1}e_\Phi L\Phi^*(v)$, not just a map with the correct finite evaluations. Here $c_\Phi$ uses derived (Pull), not underived module inverse image. The exact coefficient extension needed for (Pull) follows from [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus]: every scheme here is finite type over a field, hence noetherian, and $B=U_T$ is its allowed $\Omega_T^c$. The new normalization lemma supplies compatibility with the actual reconstructed maps through rationalization and $J$.

source.place: First sentence, the constant-object and finite-coefficient realization required for rationality

proof.text: The complex $U_Y[0]$ has only its degree-zero cohomology, which is the rank-one free coefficient module. The one-stratum stratification $Y$ therefore verifies the locally finitely presented condition in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]; isomorphism via $v$ gives bounded constructibility of $K$. Together with the invertible $\phi$ this is precisely the Weil-object input type of [nt-assume-trace-formula], without invoking that assumption's trace conclusion. The canonical derived composition comparison is [def-sfb-dc-upper-star-comp]. The unit law $e_f Lf^*(e_g)c_{f,g}=e_{gf}$ in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] and the composition clause of [lem-zl-normalized-coefficient-unit-realization] give, by induction, $v\phi_m=e_{\Phi^m}L(\Phi^m)^*(v)$ for every $m\ge1$, under those compositors. Indeed substituting the formula for $\phi$ into one additional iterate cancels $L\Phi^*(v^{-1}v)$, and the displayed unit law combines the two consecutive unit maps.

proof.text: Use in both constructions the chosen compactification $c=(j,g)$ of $a_Y$ that defines $Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek]. The finite levels of $M$ have etale origin and Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. Extension by zero leaves this bound (on the open it is the rank-one module and on its complement zero). Choose $d\ge\dim Y$. By [lem-coef-integral-compact-support], the output is integral constructible and its reductions have the common Tor bound $[0,2d]$. Thus the intermediates of $S_gJ_j$ satisfy the domain of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Its actual system realization supplies $c_V:\mathcal L_YS_gJ_j\mathcal R_YM\xrightarrow\sim Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{int},c}M$ for $V=S_gJ_j$. The specified comparison $\alpha_M:\mathcal R_Y(P_RM)\xrightarrow\sim\mathcal F(\mathcal R_YM)=S_gJ_j\mathcal R_YM$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization], together with the reconstruction unit $u_{P_RM}:P_RM\xrightarrow\sim\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_Y(P_RM)$, invertible on derived-complete objects by [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus], gives $\chi=c_V\circ\mathcal L_Y(\alpha_M)\circ u_{P_RM}:P_RM\xrightarrow\sim Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{int},c}M$. To identify the two constructions here, [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor] describes $P_R$'s strict tower: its levels are $\operatorname{Res}_n Rg_{*,n}j_!M_n$; its transition is the image of the coefficient quotient followed by the coefficient-restriction comparison. These are exactly the levels and transitions in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; the restriction comparison composes for successive quotients by [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. No faithfulness of evaluations is used. Put $N=(Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{int},c}M)[1/\ell]$. The same compact-support definition identifies $N=Ra_{Y!}E_Y$, and [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] gives $C_E=\operatorname{Fib}_sN\in D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$.

source.place: First sentence, the constant-object and finite-coefficient realization required for rationality

proof.text:
Use the specified maps $a:J_s((P_RM)[1/\ell])\xrightarrow\sim P_E^cJ_Y(E_Y)$ and $b:T^s_{E,\Omega}P_E^c\xrightarrow\sim P_\Omega^cT^Y_{E,\Omega}$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. With $T=T^s_{E,\Omega}$, let $\gamma=b_{J_Y(E_Y)}\circ T(a)$, so $\gamma:TJ_s((P_RM)[1/\ell])\xrightarrow\sim P_\Omega^cK$. This $P_\Omega^c$ is the chosen $Rg_*j_!$ module-object functor of [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek]. Let $\chi_E:(P_RM)[1/\ell]\xrightarrow\sim N$ be the rationalized comparison of Step 3. The new point comparison [lem-zl-point-realization-coefficient-comparison], applied to the adic object $N$, has target $\rho_{E,s}(\operatorname{Fib}_sN)=\rho_{E,s}(C_E)$. Specify
$$\sigma_Y=\beta_N\circ TJ_s(\chi_E)\circ\gamma^{-1}:Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{cond}}K\xrightarrow\sim\rho_{E,s}(C_E).$$
All intermediate sources and targets are now typed: $J_s$ is applied to $N$, never to the vector-space complex $C_E$. This constructs the claimed isomorphism from the exact compact-support comparisons and the missing point comparison, without an operator-compatibility claim. The cohomology and geometric-value clauses follow by applying the exact finite-matrix realization and its cohomology identification in [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace]: the result is $\rho_{E,s}(H_c^i(Y,E)[0])$ with value $H_c^i(Y,E)\otimes_E\Omega$.

proof.text:
For $x:s\to Y$, define $\lambda_x=e_x\circ Lx^*(v):Lx^*K\xrightarrow\sim U_s$. The generic normalization lemma [lem-zl-normalized-coefficient-unit-realization], now applied to $x$, identifies this with the reconstructed constant-fibre map after rationalization, $J$ and derived coefficient extension. The unit clause of [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace] identifies $U_s=\rho_{E,s}(E[0])$. Let $h=\Phi^m$ and suppose $hx=x$. Write $c_{x,h}:L(hx)^*\xrightarrow\sim Lx^*Lh^*$ for the actual derived compositor [def-sfb-dc-upper-star-comp]. Step 2 and naturality of $c$ give
$$\lambda_x\,Lx^*(\phi_m)\,c_{x,h,K}\,\lambda_x^{-1}=e_x\,Lx^*(e_h)\,c_{x,h,U_Y}\,e_x^{-1}=e_{hx}e_x^{-1}=1.$$
The middle equality is exactly the unit composition law of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]; the last uses the fixed-point equality with its canonical pullback comparison. This proves the actual stalk-operator identity. When $hx\ne x$ the same calculation relates the two different fibres, and asserts no endomorphism. The constructions prove only the object, compact-support isomorphism and fixed-stalk normalization requested here; they require no global Frobenius equality, trace or dualizability theorem.
